purpose: Define the versioned vocabulary, compatibility rules, mechanism-registration shape, and ownership boundaries for human-first sites that also expose explicit machine-readable web surfaces.

concerns.title: Readability
concerns.definition: Discovery metadata and alternate content representations that help crawlers, retrieval systems, and agents understand a human-facing site.
concerns.boundary: Readability describes content and discovery; it does not grant permission to invoke actions.

concerns.title: Capability
concerns.definition: Explicitly declared browser-agent or tool interactions together with their permissions, consent, security, audit, and revocation boundaries.
concerns.boundary: Capability declarations do not imply readability, efficiency, or commercial authority.

concerns.title: Efficiency
concerns.definition: Lower-overhead, source-equivalent representations and delivery behavior for machine consumers.
concerns.boundary: Efficiency must not weaken content meaning, access controls, provenance, or capability safeguards.

concerns.title: Commerce
concerns.definition: Machine-readable commercial meaning and the boundary around any guarded transaction-oriented capability.
concerns.boundary: Commerce classification does not authorize a transaction or define Store-owned action semantics.

site_classes.title: Web application
site_classes.definition: A site whose primary purpose is an interactive browser-delivered product or tool.

site_classes.title: Commerce site
site_classes.definition: A site whose primary purpose includes presenting products, offers, or guarded transaction paths.

site_classes.title: Content publication
site_classes.definition: A site whose primary purpose is publishing articles, media, research, or other human-readable content.

site_classes.title: Documentation site
site_classes.definition: A site whose primary purpose is structured product, project, API, or reference documentation.

site_classes.title: Hybrid site
site_classes.definition: A site with multiple first-class purposes that cannot be represented truthfully by one other stable class.

requirement_strengths.definition: An applicable site must implement the mechanism and provide current evidence.
An applicable site should implement the mechanism; an evidenced omission remains advisory rather than passing silently.
A site may implement the mechanism, and absence alone does not create a conformance failure.
The mechanism becomes required only when its explicit, machine-identified condition applies.
A site must not publish, advertise, infer, or fabricate the mechanism under the resolved profile rule.

maturity_levels.label: established web standard / broadly deployed
maturity_levels.definition: A stable web mechanism with standards-based or broadly deployed interoperability evidence.

maturity_levels.label: published industry specification
maturity_levels.definition: A mechanism described by a public primary specification but not yet established across the broader web.

maturity_levels.label: emerging convention
maturity_levels.definition: A documented convention with observable adoption whose compatibility and governance remain in motion.

maturity_levels.label: experimental/incubating capability
maturity_levels.definition: An exploratory mechanism that must not block unrelated publication or imply production readiness by default.

mechanisms.title: Optional AI crawler guidance
mechanisms.description: Product-token-specific crawl guidance expressed through the Robots Exclusion Protocol for an AI crawler whose operator publishes authoritative identification documentation.

condition.description: The site owner chooses a distinct policy for an AI crawler whose product token and purpose are documented by its operator.

content_rules.description: Every AI-specific group names a product token backed by current operator documentation and records the intended crawl purpose in review evidence.
Crawler guidance must not be represented as authentication, authorization, license, consent, or enforceable access control.
AI-specific groups use the same UTF-8, group, product-token, allow, and disallow semantics as RFC 9309.

validation_rules.description: Reject an AI-specific group when its product token cannot be traced to current operator documentation.
Reject malformed groups or rules using the RFC 9309 parsing and matching requirements.

maturity.rationale: AI-specific product tokens and purposes evolve across operators even though the underlying Robots Exclusion Protocol is standardized.

registration_evidence.description: The standards-track protocol defines product-token-specific crawler groups while explicitly excluding access authorization.

mechanisms.title: Justified AI-oriented discovery hints
mechanisms.description: Narrow machine-readable hints whose names and processing semantics are published by an identified consumer, without inventing a universal AI metadata vocabulary.

locations: consumer-specified HTML metadata or HTTP field

condition.description: A real target consumer publishes stable hint semantics and the site has an evidenced need for that consumer-specific hint.

content_rules.description: A hint must not grant capability, consent, license, transaction, or publication authority.
Do not emit guessed metadata names, values, or processing semantics without a primary consumer-owned specification.
Hint values are derived only from current public canonical content and remain subordinate to that content.

validation_rules.description: Reject a present hint without a resolvable primary specification for its exact name, value shape, and consumer.
Reject a hint that violates the syntax or extension rules of its HTML or HTTP host surface.

maturity.rationale: No cross-consumer AI hint vocabulary is established; registration is only a guarded extension point for explicitly documented consumer semantics.

registration_evidence.description: The HTML Standard requires metadata extensions to identify their keyword, semantics, specification, and status.

mechanisms.title: Canonical link metadata
mechanisms.description: A page-level canonical link relation identifying the preferred human-facing URL for duplicate or source-equivalent representations.

locations: HTML link element or HTTP Link field

condition.description: The response represents a public human-facing page that may be indexed or has duplicate or alternate representations.

content_rules.description: The target is the absolute HTTPS URL of duplicative or superset content and remains stable across alternate representations.
A machine-oriented alternate points to the human-facing page as canonical rather than replacing it as the preferred URL.
Each representation resolves to exactly one internally consistent canonical target.

validation_rules.description: Reject a target that is not duplicate, source-equivalent, or a truthful superset of the referring content.
Reject a canonical target that is malformed, inaccessible to the intended public audience, or outside an explicitly reviewed ownership boundary.
Reject conflicting canonical declarations for the same representation.

maturity.rationale: The canonical link relation is registered by RFC 6596 and broadly used by web indexing systems.

registration_evidence.description: RFC 6596 registers the canonical relation and defines its duplicate-or-superset target constraint.

mechanisms.title: cats.txt experimental well-known file
mechanisms.description: The satirical cats.txt draft served at /.well-known/cats.txt, registered only as an optional experiment rather than a web or AI interoperability standard.

condition.description: The site operator voluntarily participates and can maintain the draft's public claims without inventing feline, personal, or security data.

content_rules.description: A feline-generated key, embedding, or validation image must not be treated as authentication, cryptographic, identity, or trust authority.
Do not invent a cat, role, relationship, credential, or observation merely to satisfy the draft.
Any claims, contacts, images, or embeddings are limited to intentionally public, consented source material.

validation_rules.description: When present, validate the location, media type, and fields against the cited cats.txt draft without calling it an IETF standard.
Reject private contact data, secrets, unapproved personal data, or embeddings derived from non-public source material.
Reject a claimed cats.txt artifact served outside the origin's exact /.well-known/cats.txt path.

maturity.rationale: The publisher describes cats.txt as satirical, and its informational draft explicitly is not an Internet Standards Track specification.

registration_evidence.description: The public draft defines the experimental location and format while disclaiming Internet Standards Track status.

mechanisms.title: EntityMap HTML companion
mechanisms.description: The human- and crawler-readable HTML companion generated from a conforming entitymap.json under the EntityMap v1.0 specification.

condition.description: The same origin has voluntarily published a conforming /entitymap.json artifact.

content_rules.description: The HTML companion is generated from the same entitymap.json and is never maintained as an independent semantic source.
The document links to /entitymap.json with rel=alternate and type=application/json.
Every rendered chunk retains visible publisher attribution and its public canonical source URL.

validation_rules.description: Reject a companion whose entities, chunks, source URLs, or attribution diverge from the paired entitymap.json.
Reject a companion carrying a noindex directive contrary to the cited specification.
Reject missing visible publisher text, source links, or the required JSON alternate link.

maturity.rationale: EntityMap v1.0 publicly specifies the generated HTML companion, but broad interoperable deployment has not been established.

registration_evidence.description: The published v1.0 specification defines /entitymap.html as a generated companion with visible attribution and a JSON alternate link.

mechanisms.title: EntityMap JSON
mechanisms.description: An optional source-backed entity and evidence index at /entitymap.json following the EntityMap v1.0 industry specification.

condition.description: The publisher chooses to maintain an entity index and can derive every entity, chunk, relation, and attribution from current public canonical sources.

content_rules.description: Each chunk preserves the canonical public source URL, page title, and exact publisher attribution required by the cited specification.
Relations, confidence, verification status, and certification claims reflect review evidence and never upgrade automated inference to verified fact.
Entities and chunks contain only current public canonical material and exclude hidden, privileged, or audience-restricted content.

validation_rules.description: Reject malformed, cross-domain, expired-as-current, or otherwise unevidenced certification and verification claims; registry unavailability remains unknown.
Reject chunks whose sourceUrl is non-public, non-canonical, inaccessible to the intended audience, or materially inconsistent with the chunk.
Reject a present file that fails the EntityMap v1.0 structural, attribution, predicate, or size constraints.

maturity.rationale: EntityMap has a public v1.0 specification and validator, while broad deployment and independent interoperability evidence remain unestablished.

registration_evidence.description: The published v1.0 specification defines the JSON structure, source attribution, freshness, and validation requirements.

mechanisms.title: Aggregate llms-full.txt representation
mechanisms.description: An optional Markdown aggregation of a bounded public documentation corpus, treated as an emerging implementation convention rather than part of the llms.txt v2 proposal.

condition.description: The site has a bounded public documentation corpus that can be aggregated within an owned size budget without leaking excluded content.

content_rules.description: The publisher declares and enforces a size budget; oversized corpora use selective linked Markdown rather than an unbounded aggregate.
The aggregate includes only current public canonical documentation and preserves page boundaries and source URLs.
Every included section is generated from the same reviewed source revision as its human-facing page without machine-only claims or instructions.

validation_rules.description: Reject a present aggregate with material additions, omissions, changed claims, stale pages, or missing canonical source links.
Reject hidden, draft, authenticated, tenant-specific, personal, or otherwise non-public content.
Reject a present aggregate that exceeds the publisher's explicit machine-consumption size budget.

maturity.rationale: Documentation platforms publish llms-full.txt, but the current llms.txt v2 proposal does not define it and interoperable limits remain unsettled.

registration_evidence.description: Mintlify documents automatic llms-full.txt publication as a complete documentation-site Markdown aggregation.

mechanisms.title: llms.txt curated discovery index
mechanisms.description: A concise, path-scoped Markdown overview and curated link index following the llms.txt v2 proposal.

condition.description: The site or controlled path exposes public content for which a maintained, curated agent-readable overview provides a truthful navigation benefit.

content_rules.description: The H1, summary, guidance, sections, and links describe only the site or path covered by the file and follow the v2 ordering rules.
Linked resources are intentionally public, canonical, current, and preferably source-equivalent Markdown when available.
The file provides navigation context only and never claims crawler permission, training consent, access authorization, or action capability.

validation_rules.description: Reject broken, non-public, misleading, or out-of-scope links that are not explicitly justified external context.
Reject a present file without the required H1 or with headings and link lists that violate the cited v2 format.
Reject ambiguous path coverage; the most specific applicable llms.txt governs its descendant path.

maturity.rationale: The v2 proposal records substantial implementation adoption, while its governance remains an open community proposal rather than a web standard.

registration_evidence.description: The August 2026 v2 proposal defines path scope, ordered Markdown format, alternate discovery, and current adoption evidence.

mechanisms.title: Source-equivalent Markdown alternate
mechanisms.description: An explicitly discoverable Markdown representation of a canonical human-facing page, derived from the same reviewed source without semantic drift.

condition.description: A public canonical page has a reviewed source from which a current, materially equivalent Markdown representation can be generated without exposing hidden or privileged content.

content_rules.description: The alternate identifies the human-facing canonical URL and is discoverable from that canonical representation with an alternate link typed text/markdown.
The alternate applies the same or stricter access controls and contains no hidden, private, draft, or privileged source material.
The alternate and canonical page derive from the same reviewed source revision with no material additions, omissions, or changed claims.

validation_rules.description: Reject a present alternate that lacks a typed HTML or HTTP Link relation from the canonical page or lacks its canonical backlink.
Reject user-agent sniffing, Markdown preference ties, missing Vary: Accept, or missing Content-Location when the canonical URL performs negotiation.
Reject a present alternate whose source revision, freshness, meaning, provenance, or access controls do not satisfy the profile-wide representation policy.

maturity.rationale: The Markdown media type and alternate links are standardized, while a web-wide convention for source-equivalent page alternates and deterministic Markdown negotiation remains emerging.

registration_evidence.description: RFC 8288 defines typed alternate links, providing the standards basis for explicit discovery without user-agent inference.

mechanisms.title: Robots Exclusion Protocol
mechanisms.description: Origin-scoped crawler access guidance published at /robots.txt under RFC 9309, separate from authorization and privacy controls.

condition.description: The profile applies to an HTTP origin that publishes public resources for crawler discovery or indexing.

content_rules.description: The file states crawl guidance only; it is not access authorization, authentication, confidentiality protection, training consent, or action permission.
User-agent groups, allow and disallow rules, matching, encoding, retrieval, and caching follow RFC 9309.
Rules must not disclose non-public paths or secrets that are not otherwise intentionally public.

validation_rules.description: Reject a present file whose encoding, group parsing, rule matching, redirect handling, or status behavior contradicts RFC 9309.
Reject claims that robots.txt protects private resources or grants permissions beyond crawler access guidance.

maturity.rationale: RFC 9309 standardizes the long-deployed Robots Exclusion Protocol and its crawler interoperability behavior.

registration_evidence.description: RFC 9309 publishes the standards-track syntax, matching, retrieval, and security boundaries for /robots.txt.

mechanisms.title: XML Sitemap
mechanisms.description: A current XML inventory of canonical public URLs and optional discovery metadata under the Sitemaps protocol.

condition.description: The origin exposes canonical public URLs intended for discovery and can generate a truthful current inventory.

content_rules.description: Every entry is an absolute canonical URL intentionally public on the allowed host and does not reveal private, preview, session, or internal routes.
Optional last-modified values reflect actual significant source changes; priority and change frequency are omitted unless truthfully maintained.
Encoding, escaping, host scope, file limits, and sitemap-index partitioning follow the Sitemaps protocol.

validation_rules.description: Reject stale, broken, redirected-away, non-canonical, private, or cross-host URLs not permitted by the protocol.
Reject malformed XML or a sitemap that violates protocol encoding, namespace, location, size, URL-count, or host constraints.

maturity.rationale: The Sitemaps protocol is a stable, broadly deployed search-engine discovery mechanism with published interoperability rules.

registration_evidence.description: The published protocol defines URL-set, sitemap-index, encoding, host, size, and discovery constraints.

mechanisms.title: JSON-LD structured discovery metadata
mechanisms.description: Standards-based JSON-LD embedded in a canonical page to describe visible public entities and relationships for discovery, without defining commerce or action semantics.

condition.description: The canonical page presents public facts that an authoritative, stable vocabulary can describe truthfully without fabricating entities, relationships, offers, actions, or credentials.

content_rules.description: Entity identifiers and URLs resolve to canonical public resources and remain stable across equivalent representations.
Structured claims are current, source-backed, and materially visible on the canonical page; hidden, private, inferred, or placeholder claims are prohibited.
This checkpoint does not use structured metadata to grant actions or define seller, advertising, offer, payment, fulfillment, or transaction semantics.
The document is valid JSON-LD 1.1 and uses authoritative vocabulary terms whose meaning matches the visible facts.

validation_rules.description: Reject invalid JSON-LD or unresolved, redefined, or semantically incompatible contexts and terms.
Reject metadata that is stale, contradicts the page, invents facts, exposes non-public data, or claims capabilities and commerce semantics outside this checkpoint.

maturity.rationale: JSON-LD 1.1 is a W3C Recommendation and Schema.org supplies a broadly deployed discovery vocabulary, while vocabulary-specific conformance remains independently governed.

authoritative_references.title: Getting started with schema.org using Microdata

registration_evidence.description: The W3C Recommendation defines interoperable JSON-LD 1.1 syntax and processing.
Schema.org publishes implementation guidance for embedding shared structured vocabulary in web content.

compatibility.same_major_guarantee: Existing valid core records retain their identifiers and meaning unless a documented major-version migration replaces them.
additive_changes: clarify non-normative prose without changing validation
add optional mechanism records without changing existing identifiers or meaning
add core site classes, requirement strengths, or maturity levels in a reviewed minor version without changing existing values
register namespaced optional extensions that do not affect core conformance
breaking_changes: remove or rename a core concern, site class, requirement strength, maturity level, or mechanism
change lifecycle, requirement, maturity, or concern meaning
make previously optional data required or relax prohibited behavior
change concern assignment, reference or evidence shape, extension isolation, or ownership boundaries

allowed: add stricter validation owned by the extension namespace
prohibited: redefine core concern, site-class, requirement-strength, maturity, lifecycle, reference, evidence, or compatibility semantics
satisfy a core requirement with an unknown extension
grant capability, consent, publication, deployment, or transaction authority
move ownership away from the canonical repository

hygiene.owns: The canonical profile, core vocabulary, lifecycle, schema, compatibility policy, extension rules, and reference validation.
hygiene.excludes: Artifact generation, reusable workflow implementation, fleet rollout, commerce-domain action contracts, conformance dashboards, and site publication.

holon.owns: Deterministic generation for new repositories and sites from an accepted, immutably pinned profile.
holon.excludes: Profile meaning, existing-fleet mutation, site facts, and final publication authority.

relay.owns: Reusable validation and publication workflow execution plus evidence transport for pinned profile consumers.
relay.excludes: Profile semantics, site-class selection, commerce semantics, credentials, and final publication decisions.

pace.owns: Previewed, reversible migration and convergence pull requests for existing sites after the profile is accepted.
pace.excludes: Direct default-branch mutation, policy definition, and automatic adoption claims.

store.owns: Transaction-domain semantics and guarded commerce capability contracts introduced by separately reviewed later work.
store.excludes: The core publication profile, non-commerce concerns, fabricated seller relationships, and authorization inferred from metadata.

observatory.owns: Collection and reporting of privacy-safe conformance evidence and metrics for an accepted profile.
observatory.excludes: Policy definition, remediation, rollout, passing-state fabrication, and site mutation.
